memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not worship any other god, for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.'" - Exod 34:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jealousy sounds like a flaw in us, so this verse can unsettle people. But there is a jealousy that is not petty — it is right.

A husband who feels nothing when his wife is unfaithful does not love her. Indifference is not virtue. God's jealousy is the fierce commitment of a love that will not share what belongs exclusively to it. He is jealous *for* us, not *of* us.

That is why Scripture so often uses marriage language for God and His people. Israel's idolatry is called adultery, not merely bad policy. And the New Testament carries this forward: Christ loves the church as a husband loves his bride, and gave Himself up for her (Eph 5:25). Paul says he feels a godly jealousy for the church, wanting to present her as a pure bride to Christ (2 Cor 11:2).

So when God says "worship no other god," He is not being insecure. He is being faithful. He knows that anything else we put in His place will eventually consume us, because nothing else can carry the weight of our worship.

Ask yourself what has been quietly claiming your deepest loyalty. Your work. Your reputation. Your family. Your comfort. God's jealousy is His refusal to let you settle for any of them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What competes with God for first place in your heart?
2. Does God's jealousy feel threatening to you, or protective?
3. How does knowing Christ as the Bridegroom change how you see this?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You will not share my heart with rivals, and I am glad. Root out everything that competes with You. Amen.
